questions.learningObjective: Interpret character motives, political conflict and dramatic presentation in Act 1 of Antony and Cleopatra using the play as evidence.
questions.prompt: In Shakespeare’s Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1, scene 1: Philo contrasts Antony’s former soldierly gaze with his present attention to Cleopatra. What does this opening contrast establish?
questions.answer: A Roman soldier’s critical view of Antony’s changed priorities.
options: Cleopatra’s admission that she intends to abandon Antony.
An impartial verdict delivered by the play’s narrator.
A Roman soldier’s critical view of Antony’s changed priorities.
Caesar’s direct account of Antony’s recent battles.
questions.explanation: Philo speaks as Antony’s dissatisfied follower. His military comparison introduces a judgement that the action will complicate; it is not an omniscient narration.

questions.prompt: In Shakespeare’s Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1, scene 1: Why does Antony resist Cleopatra’s invitation to state how much he loves her?
questions.answer: He presents genuine love as exceeding measurable limits.
options: He presents genuine love as exceeding measurable limits.
He insists that Rome must first authorise their relationship.
He thinks affection can be settled by a territorial survey.
He cannot remember the value of a promised gift.
questions.explanation: Antony associates a love that can be reckoned with poverty and imagines new heaven and earth. The exaggeration makes measurement inadequate to his claim.

Military discipline has ended Cleopatra’s political influence.
His concern for Roman citizens outweighs his attachment.

questions.prompt: In Shakespeare’s Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1, scene 2: The Soothsayer says Charmian will outlive her mistress. In light of the ending, what is the strongest reading of this prediction?
questions.answer: It is fulfilled narrowly, without promising Charmian a long surviving life.

It guarantees Charmian will inherit Cleopatra’s throne.
It proves Charmian will leave Egypt before the final defeat.

questions.answer: Absence makes him reassess what he had wished to lose.

She thinks habitual opposition may drive Antony away.

questions.prompt: In Shakespeare’s Antony and Cleopatra, Act 1, scene 4: Caesar recalls Antony’s endurance during earlier campaigns while censuring his life in Egypt. What is the effect of this recollection?
questions.answer: It makes Antony’s apparent decline more striking by recalling his capacity.

It makes Antony’s apparent decline more striking by recalling his capacity.
It establishes that Caesar personally witnessed every hardship described.
It removes every political disagreement between the triumvirs.
questions.explanation: The account of remarkable endurance supplies a demanding contrast to present indulgence. Caesar can recognise Antony’s past greatness while condemning his current conduct.

questions.prompt: In Shakespeare’s Antony and Cleopatra, Act 2, scene 2: What political purpose does Agrippa assign to Antony’s marriage to Octavia?
questions.answer: It could bind Caesar and Antony through a family relationship.
